source: Native AWS CLI observations. Scenarios replay public requests and compare state/configuration after deliberate local ticks, not AWS scheduling latency.

reference_claims.user_guide_retrieved: AWS/DynamoDB defaults to ignore missing data; explicitly allows override.
reference_claims.api_reference_retrieved: AWS/DynamoDB always ignores missing data even if a different TreatMissingData is chosen.
reference_claims.pinned_model_treat_missing_data_document:
Sets how this alarm is to handle missing data points. If TreatMissingData is omitted, the default behavior of missing is used. For more information, see Configuring How CloudWatch Alarms Treats Missing Data.

Valid Values: breaching | notBreaching | ignore | missing

Alarms that evaluate metrics in the AWS/DynamoDB namespace always ignore missing data even if you choose a different option for TreatMissingData. When an AWS/DynamoDB metric has missing data, alarms that evaluate that metric remain in their current state.

This parameter is not applicable to PromQL alarms.

limitations: No metric samples are published; metric identities are unique and unpublished.
Stable manual states without a subsequent evaluator queryDate are bounded non-observations, not proof evaluation ran.
Period 10 is deliberately valid but high-resolution; no conclusion about a published DynamoDB metric or ordinary 60-second cadence.
History requests are exact-alarm scoped, nonpaginated MaxRecords=100; any NextToken is a retained truncation limitation.
The ordinary namespace is a missing-data control, not a service-owned metric.
API/model and current user guide disagree; experimental results take precedence only within observed scope.
No custom metric publication or DynamoDB resources.
Stable manual state is a bounded non-observation, not an independent evaluator queryDate.
Only these arithmetic and used/unused namespace combinations are exercised.
Comparisons preserve state and omitted versus explicit TreatMissingData. Native queryDate/history is retained separately; local ticks are not those native query times.
The mixed-namespace arithmetic captures show that an unused ordinary MetricStat disables the DynamoDB default. No dependency-only namespace inference is used.
